args.topic: Stoic agency and boundaries around demanding people
args.persona: A calm, measured voice that speaks like a trusted mentor sitting across a firelit table — unhurried, thoughtful, and deeply grounded in ancient wisdom applied to modern struggle.
args.scriptExcerpt:
The modern world has completely misunderstood what it means to be a Stoic. It is not about enduring bad behavior in silence.

People think resilience means standing like a stone statue while a frantic relative chips away at your sanity. That is not philosophy. That is just self-destruction. Real Stoicism is deeply active. When Epictetus taught his students in Nicopolis two thousand years ago, he did not tell them to absorb the chaos of others. He taught them how to ruthlessly cut off the supply. You possess a specific type of inner agency that demanding people rely on. Once you learn to recognize the exact moment they ask for it, you can simply refuse to hand it over.
